title: Module quiz: Scenario: agentic tool builder

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: an agent that writes and proposes its own tools, which a gate reviews before anything runs. A tool's code opens a file for writing, while the proposal declares only reading, and the policy sends writes to a person. What does the gate do?

options.text: Refuses it, since an effect nobody mentioned cannot be approved on its behalf
Sends it back for a revision of the description, since the declaration is thin
options.says: Ruled out because an undeclared effect is one of the refusals and not a matter of the description: "Three things refuse a proposal." and "Its code shows a permission that the proposal did not declare"

options.text: Approves it behind a gate, since the policy already covers writes
options.says: Ruled out because the gate approves only what was declared: "Its code shows a permission that the proposal did not declare, which is the case of a tool that says it reads and fetches a page."

options.text: Approves it outright, since the proposal declares a permission that the policy allows
options.says: Ruled out because a declared read does not cover the write the code shows: "Its code shows a permission that the proposal did not declare", and a refusal wins: "A proposal with a refusal is refused, whatever else is true of it."

origin.section: What is refused, and what is only sent back

questions.stem: Scenario: an agent that writes and proposes its own tools, which a gate reviews before anything runs. A team proposes to run generated tools in a container and to drop the gate, because the container limits the damage. Which gap remains?

options.text: Nothing, because a container makes every tool safe to run
options.says: Ruled out because a container is only one of the five jobs: "Containment is the environment's job."

options.text: Nothing checks what the code does against what was declared
options.says: The container holds the run, and only the gate compares the code with its declaration.

options.text: The container's memory limit, which the gate cannot read
options.says: Ruled out because the gate reads and flags the limits: "a timeout above the limit and a memory request above the limit".

options.text: The tool's network access, which the container cannot limit
options.says: Ruled out because the container already closes it (page 1): "The container has no internet access".

origin.section: A text scan is not a sandbox

questions.stem: Scenario: an agent that writes and proposes its own tools, which a gate reviews before anything runs. Which record satisfies the audit part of the design?

options.text: A file that the agent keeps and updates for itself after every one of its runs
options.says: Ruled out because an editable file is not an audit: "A log that the agent can edit is not an audit."

options.text: A summary that the agent writes by itself at the end of each working day
options.says: Ruled out because a summary by the agent is its own account: "The record has to be written by the gate and the runner and kept where the agent has no write access".

options.text: One line per run, kept in the folder where the agent saves its tools
options.says: Ruled out because the agent can write where the log is kept: "kept where the agent has no write access".

options.text: One line per decision and per run, kept where its subject has no access
options.says: The audit is kept out of the agent's reach.

questions.stem: Scenario: an agent that writes and proposes its own tools, which a gate reviews before anything runs. A proposed name is 64 characters of lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. What does the gate do with the name?

options.text: Flags it, since the longest name has to leave a spare character
options.says: Ruled out because the length is allowed: "A name may be 64 characters long, and 65 is too long."

options.text: Flags it, because names this long are hard for the model to choose
options.says: Ruled out because the gate checks the form and not the model's taste: "Four things only send it back: a name that is not in the fixed form".

options.text: Accepts it, as it sits at the ceiling for such labels and not above it
Accepts it, since the description also has at least 64 words
options.says: Ruled out because the description has its own minimum: "The description needs at least the minimum number of words, and exactly the minimum is enough."
